Microsoft Copilot Expands: Multi-Model Research Available Now, Cowork and Skills Going GA This Month

By Will Zheng · April 6, 2026 · From Issue #5

Microsoft / VentureBeat / Crescendo AI Industry

Microsoft is quietly assembling the most comprehensive AI workspace platform in enterprise, and this week's releases accelerate that. Multi-model Deep Research is now broadly available in Copilot — users can select which model performs the research, with GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1, and Grok 4 all accessible from within the same interface. Copilot Cowork — the persistent, multi-agent workspace that lets teams spin up AI collaborators alongside human ones — is expected to go generally available by end of April, alongside Copilot Skills, which enables organizations to build, publish, and deploy custom AI capabilities into the Copilot surface without writing integration code. The "Council" feature currently in early access lets users run the same prompt through multiple models side-by-side for comparison. Deeper write and action integrations with Box, Notion, Linear, and Dropbox are also rolling out — not just read access, but the ability to create, edit, and complete tasks. For enterprise buyers, the strategic read is clear: Microsoft is closing the loop between model capability, agent execution, and productivity surface inside a single governed platform. The consolidation risk for IT decision-makers is real.
